subject: Matrix with asymmetrical factorr data generation

messages.author: 63780e17e344f0aa
messages.subject: Matrix with asymmetrical factorr data generation
parts:
Hi,

How to generate the factor variance and error covariance and factor mean data for matrix with asymmetrical  factors?


I have a matrix script, and the data is not generation according to the matrix. I am providing the script.


have a matrix structure like this
Construct 1: 6 items
Construct 2: 9 items
Construct 3: 10 items
Construct 4; 7 items
Construct 5; 4 items
Construct 6: 10 items

Is there any general syntax for factor variance and error covariance and factor mean data in simsem? The documentation on simsem.org is bit rigid in terms of varieties of example in context of asymmetrical matrices.


=================================================================================

==
Asymmetrical Matrix
=================================================================================

==

loadingVal <- matrix(0, 34, 6)
loadingVal[1:5, 1] <- c(1,0.6, 0.7,0.6,0.7)
loadingVal[6:11, 2] <- c(1,1.1, 0.9,0.9,0.7,0.8)
loadingVal[12:17, 3] <- c(1,1.2, 1.1,0.8,0.3,0.5)
loadingVal[18:22, 4] <- c(1,1.1, 0.4, 0.3,0.9)
loadingVal[23:25, 5] <- c(1,1.1, 1.2)
loadingVal[26:34, 6] <- c(1,0.5, 1.0,0.5,0.5,0.9,07,0.7,0.7)

LY <- simsem::bind(loadingVal, "runif(1, 0.4, 0.9)")

factor.mean <- rep(NA, 6)
factor.mean.starting <- c(2,3,3,3,3,2)
AL <- simsem::bind(factor.mean, factor.mean.starting)

W <- matrix(NA, 6, 6)
W <- diag(c(1,1,1,1,1,1))
W[lower.tri(W)] <- c(0.4, 0.3, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2,0.4, 0.3, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2,0.3, 0.3, 0.2)
BE <- simsem::bind(W )

RPS <-simsem::bind(diag(6),symmetric = TRUE)

RTE <-simsem::bind(diag(34),symmetric = TRUE)

CFA.Model <- simsem::model(LY=LY, BE=BE, RPS=RPS, RTE=RTE, AL= AL ,modelType="CFA)
data <- simsem::generate(CFA.Model, 410)

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Matrix with asymmetrical factorr data generation
parts:
Well, you can't generate data with ones on the diagonal of the beta matrix so that would need to be fixed regardless. Looking at your code, the other issue is probably the specification of RTS and RPS in the model command. These specifying the correlation matrices of the latent variables and the observed variables, which simsem attempt to translate into covariance matrices. For simple models this works well, for a more complex model this occasionally has issues (specifically combinations of the beta and lambda matrix might imply negative population variances). I think that's what's happening here. If you change the sim command to use the given psi and theta matrices as covariance matrices (see below) things work fine. 

CFA.Model <- simsem::model(LY=LY, BE=BE, PS=RPS, TE=RTE, AL= AL ,modelType="SEM")

One issue (not sure if it is the only one). Is the 1s on the diagonal of the beta matrix. This should be a matrix of regression among latent variables, a 1 on the diagonal implies a regression path from a latent variable back to itself. Replace the 1's on the diagonal of the beta matrix with 0s.
